overall.sentence: Pulsed-field, angle-resolved resistivity of UTe2 across the SC3 window was already measured and analysed with a Fermi-liquid A coefficient (Knafo et al. 2020, cited; Thebault et al. 2022 and May 2025, not cited), and the 2025 paper already reports scattering enhanced at 30-40 degrees coinciding with SC3; what is new here is the T-linear exponent and the Planckian-rate estimate.

assessment.claim: 1-2: T-linear resistivity (n near 1) with A enhanced over an order of magnitude, confined near 35 degrees and encompassing SC3 (headline: 'a new setting for Planckian strange metallicity')
assessment.note: Same system and method (pulsed-field resistivity rotated in the b-c plane) and the same finding of enhanced scattering at 30-40 degrees coinciding with SC3 appear in Thebault et al. (posted days earlier) and, at about 27 degrees, in Knafo et al. 2020 [42]; both fit Fermi-liquid T^2, so the new part is the T-linear exponent map.

assessment.claim: 3: scattering at the Planckian rate, alpha = 1.3 +/- 0.6, adding high-field UTe2 to the list of Planckian metals
assessment.note: No precedent found in the paper's references and 10 arXiv searches (2026-11-22): no earlier paper reports a Planckian or T-linear scattering rate in UTe2.

assessment.claim: 4: first association of T-linear resistivity with a spin-triplet superconducting state
assessment.note: Bastien et al. 2016 report resistivity linear in T around the ferromagnetic critical pressure of UCoGe, a candidate p-wave (spin-triplet) superconductor that superconducts there; the general 'not previously associated' statement does not hold as worded.

positioning: The paper sits on a well-measured normal state: pulsed-field resistivity of UTe2 in tilted fields was analysed by the Grenoble/Toulouse groups with a Fermi-liquid A coefficient, including a May 2025 preprint that already ties an enhanced A at 30-40 degrees to SC3 and to quantum-critical fluctuations. What this paper adds, as far as the searches show, is a map of the resistivity exponent showing n near 1 rather than 2 in that window, and an estimate that the slope is Planckian. Its claim that T-linear resistivity has never accompanied spin-triplet superconductivity is contradicted by T-linear resistivity in UCoGe under pressure, and the closest same-system transport work should be cited and reconciled with the n = 1 result.

issues.claim: T-linear resistivity has not previously been associated with a spin-triplet superconducting state.
issues.headline: T-linear resistivity already reported in triplet candidate UCoGe
issues.issue: Bastien et al. (arXiv:1608.01949, 2016) report resistivity varying linearly with temperature around the critical pressure of UCoGe, a candidate p-wave ferromagnetic superconductor that superconducts in that pressure range. The statement that T-linear resistivity has never been associated with a spin-triplet state is therefore contradicted as worded; the paper does not cite this work.

evidence.quote: although T-linear resistivity often accompanies even-parity superconductivity (6), it has not previously been associated with a spin-triplet superconductive state.

issues.fix: Cite the UCoGe pressure study and narrow the statement to what is new here: T-linear, Planckian resistivity tied to a field-induced triplet phase inside a spin-polarized state.

edit.before: although T-linear resistivity often accompanies even-parity superconductivity (6), it has not previously been associated with a spin-triplet superconductive state.
edit.after: although T-linear resistivity most often accompanies even-parity superconductivity (6), it has rarely been associated with a spin-triplet superconductive state, a notable case being UCoGe near its ferromagnetic critical pressure, and never with a field-induced triplet phase.

issues.claim: The T-linear region with A over an order of magnitude larger than at low field is confined near 35 degrees and coincides with SC3.
issues.headline: Same-system pulsed-field resistivity studies found enhanced Fermi-liquid A instead
issues.issue: Thebault et al. (arXiv:2505.09351, posted days before this paper) measured pulsed-field resistivity rotated in the b-c plane and found the A coefficient enhanced at 30-40 degrees, coinciding with SC3; Thebault et al. 2022 (arXiv:2205.15789) and Knafo et al. 2020 ([42]) analysed the same normal state with Fermi-liquid T^2 fits. None is discussed where the paper states its result, and readers will ask why they saw T^2 where this paper sees n = 1.
